- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline at 10–15% below peak, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is trending up, model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 20-day moving average for 5+ days, model tends to overpredict decline — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 7–10 days) — reduce first 5–7 days by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3–5 days if sentiment drops below -0.30.
- Avoid forecasting “flat” or “no change” when sentiment is volatile — model underestimates volatility — add 1–3% noise or ±2% range to forecast if sentiment swings >0.20.
